name: AI Deep Dive — ASML — 2026-05-02
rationale: ASML holds a structural monopoly on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, the critical bottleneck technology required for all leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing. This gives them immense pricing power, reflected in their highly stable ~30% net margins. However, with a trailing P/E of ~47x and a market cap of $550B, the market is pricing in flawless execution of the next-generation High-NA EUV rollout alongside sustained strong demand from foundries. At a conservative base case valuation of $1220.98, the stock is currently slightly overvalued (-14.4% downside) and offers no margin of safety. SELL.

bear.rationale: Growth slows to 10% as China export restrictions bite and leading-edge foundry capex cools. Net margins compress to 25% due to underutilized capacity and high R&D costs for next-gen tools. The exit P/E compresses to 20x, a more typical multiple for semi-cap equipment during a downcycle. The 1.1x quality multiplier acknowledges their monopoly but reflects the severe macro/geopolitical constraints.
risks: Geopolitical tensions lead to stricter export bans to China, severely limiting addressable market
Foundries (TSMC, Samsung, Intel) delay leading-edge node buildouts due to macro weakness

base.rationale: Growth of 15% assumes smooth execution of the High-NA EUV rollout and continued strong demand for DUV systems. Net margin remains steady at 30%, reflecting strong pricing power. The exit P/E of 28x is a premium multiple for semi-cap equipment, justified by their monopoly status. A high quality multiplier of 1.25x is applied due to their absolute monopoly on the most critical technology in modern manufacturing.
risks: High-NA EUV adoption is slower than expected due to astronomical tool costs
Valuation remains highly vulnerable to any cyclical downturn in the broader semi market

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Global 'fab on-shoring' subsidies (CHIPS Act, EU Chips Act) trigger an unprecedented, state-sponsored semi-cap spending spree that ignores traditional supply/demand cycles. Growth accelerates to a 20% CAGR. High-NA EUV carries massive margins, pushing overall net margin to 33%. The exit P/E expands to 35x. The maximum 1.30x quality multiplier reflects their status as the most strategically important company in the global semiconductor supply chain.
risks: Priced for perfection; any supply chain disruption could derail growth targets

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: Used 385.4M (shares_diluted). API provided matching figures for outstanding and diluted. No discrepancies.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 29.4% used as the anchor. Margins are extremely stable for a hardware manufacturer (26.5% -> 28.4% -> 26.7% -> 29.4%), reflecting deep structural pricing power. Base case holds this at 30%.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 revenue implies 19.1% growth ($38.9B vs $32.6B TTM), Y2 implies 20.7%. Blended consensus ~20%. Base case growth set more conservatively to 15% to account for cyclicality and the law of large numbers.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Semiconductors / Semi-Cap Equipment: median P/E 20, best-in-class 30+. Used 28x for base case due to absolute monopoly status.
dataQualityFlags: No anomalies detected. Financial data is exceptionally clean and consistent.
